name: Nasal reconstruction with skin flaps in India
summary: Indian surgeons rebuilt cut-off noses with flaps of the patient's own skin, a method described in the Sushruta Samhita and taken up by European surgeons after 1794.
description: The compendium attributed to Sushruta describes rebuilding a severed nose with a flap of living skin cut from the cheek to the size of a leaf template. In 1793 two English physicians of the East India Company reported a nose rebuilt with a forehead flap by an Indian healer; the account reached London in 1794, and in 1814 Joseph Carpue performed the operation there.

impact.note: It served one profession and its patients in India and later in Europe and America, gave them a new capability (rebuilding a lost nose from the patient's own skin), and the forehead flap it passed on remains a foundation of nasal reconstruction and of the flap surgery that grew from it.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Date the nose-repair passage itself: read Wujastyk and colleagues, On the Plastic Surgery of the Ears and Nose: The Nepalese Version of the Susrutasamhita (Heidelberg, 2023, open access but closed to the fetcher), and Meulenbeld. The years -300 to -1 render Britannica's 'last centuries BCE' and are not a range the source gives.
Check whether a written flap repair in another tradition (for example Celsus, first century CE) predates the datable form of the Sushruta passage; if so, first_known must change.
The cataract couching claim has no source; check the Sushruta Samhita's ophthalmic chapters and the history of couching, and make it a separate record if it holds.

The review gives both 1793 and 1794 for the witnessed operation, places the Madras Gazette 'in Bombay' and spells one witness 'Frindlay' (the literature has Thomas Cruso and James Findlay, and Pune as the place); confirm from the Gentleman's Magazine text before adding the witnesses or a precise place.
The Sushruta Samhita describes a cheek flap and the 1793 operation used a forehead flap; how and when the forehead method arose in India is not sourced.

research.note: The review states that the idea of using a cheek flap to create a nose was first recorded in India, but it assumes a date of 600 BC; with the text dated to the last centuries BCE or later, first_known holds only if the passage belongs to the compendium's early layer and no other tradition wrote down a flap repair before it.
